observations.behavior: Adds a project-scoping filter to DesktopFileSystemViewSet that excludes personal-space rows unless created by the requesting user.
observations.posthog_connection: Protects desktop file system entries under paths like 'me' or 'me/*' from being returned in shared team queries; relevant for users and admins accessing desktop-specific resources.

observations.behavior: Adds tests asserting that folders with path='me', their children, instruction counts, and detail views are not accessible when authenticated as another user (even staff).
observations.posthog_connection: Validates that the access control implemented in P1.F1.H1 correctly hides private me-folder content across list, parent-child, count, and retrieval endpoints.

observations.behavior: Includes cleanup behavior where deleting an owned folder does not remove its dependent child records, preserving orphaned data rather than cascading deletion.
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies ownership-dependent lifecycle: removing a creator's root entry leaves associated metadata intact if no other owner exists, potentially affecting storage and recovery expectations.

observations.limitations: Only three hunks provided. No changes to backend implementation of personal-space checks outside this viewset were shown, so broader enforcement is unverified. No migration or permission-group changes appear.

review.limitations: Only three hunks provided. No changes to backend implementation of personal-space checks outside this viewset were shown, so broader enforcement is unverified. No migration or permission-group changes appear.
review.reason: The change adds substantive project-scoping and privacy protection for desktop file system entries under personal paths, including both implementation and comprehensive API-access assertions. This could prevent unintended exposure of shared-team resources while remaining bounded to DesktopFileSystemViewSet.
review.posthog_relevance: Relevant to PostHog users who rely on desktop-specific features; protects against accidental leakage of personal workspace items within team-shared queries.
review.uncertainty: Assessment relies solely on supplied chunk; absence of related migrations or permission-layer updates may leave edge cases unchecked.
